senses.gloss: m.(b. h. שְׁוַר; v., however , Fl. to Levy Talm. Dict. IV, p. 680) ox.
units: B. Kam. 65ᵇ ש׳ בן יומו קרוי ש׳ an ox on the day of his birth is called shor (by ref. to Lev. XXII, 27). Ib. I, 1 הש׳ damage done by an ox (Ex. XXI, 28; XXII, 4). Ib. IV, 7 ש׳ המדבר the ox of the desert (aurochs, being ownerless).
<cite ref="Mishnah Kilayim 8:6">Kil. VIII, 6</cite>; <cite ref="Chullin 80a:19">Ḥull. 80ᵃ</cite> <he>בר</he>(<cite ref="E00000"><he>ה</he></cite>) <he>ש׳</he> wild ox, aurochs; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Eruvin 53b:11">Erub. 53ᵇ</cite> (in enigmatic speech) <he>ש׳ משפט</he> (not <he>במשפט</he>) = <he>תור דין</he> = <he>תְּרָדִין</he>, v. <cite ref="V00948"><he>תְּרָדָא</he> I</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="U00357"><he>שְׁוָורִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="U00357"><he>שְׁוָורִין</he></cite>, <he>שְׁוָר׳</he>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 75:13">Gen. R. s. 75</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 32:6">Gen. XXXII, 6</cite>) <he>משור אחד יצאו ש׳ הרבה</he> from the one ox (which I originally possessed) many oxen went forth.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 3:8">B. Kam. III, 8</cite>. Y. Gitt. IX, 46ᵈ bot.; a. fr.
